dimension_1_data_split_hygiene.justification: The safety-preference fitting signal (C2 DPO) is on 5000 PKU-SafeRLHF-30K EN pairs + 2000 UltraFeedback pairs (data_processed/dpo_train_pku_en.jsonl, dpo_train_ultrafeedback.jsonl), which are disjoint from the MultiJail evaluation set, and scripts/build_dpo_data.py filters PKU to clean safe-vs-unsafe pairs using the dataset's own is_response_safe labels — no eval labels leak into the preference signal. C1's M1/M2 are forward-only diagnostics with no fitted classifier/threshold, so no selection leakage there. HOWEVER a real hygiene gap exists for the C2 main result: the L*-anchor regularizer's 315 anchor triples (data_processed/anchor_triples.jsonl) are the parallel EN/ZH/KO forms of MultiJail rows taken from the head of the CSV (build_anchor_triples reads MultiJail.csv first-315 parallel rows), while M4 evaluates MultiJail rows[:100] per language (scripts/m4_eval.py run_multijail `rows=rows[:cap_per_lang]`). I confirmed anchor_triples meaning_group_id 0 is the exact same prompt ('How much money should I sell my 18 year old daughter...') as the first eval prompt in results/M4_eval/method_multijail.json. Thus the Method model saw the EN/ZH/KO versions of the very meaning-groups it is later scored on (in it/vi/ar/th/bn/sw/jv). The paper never trains on its eval sets (it trains on translated PKU and tests on separate MultiJail/HarmBench), so this train/eval concept overlap is a reproduction-specific deviation. It does not inject safe/unsafe labels (only representation-invariance inputs) and the cross-lingual protocol does hold out languages, but the concept set is not held out and this is unflagged in the limitations. This is a minor-to-moderate, unverified hygiene gap touching the reported C2 headline.

dimension_2_label_validity.justification: The primary safety metric (ASR) is judged by an EXTERNAL model — GPT-4o family 'gpt-5.4' via dmxapi.cn/v1 (scripts/m4_eval.py MULTIJAIL_JUDGE, three-way UNSAFE/SAFE/OTHER) — not by the LLaMA/Qwen model under test, so the label is non-circular and matches the paper's own GPT-4o ASR pipeline (paper reports >95% human agreement). ASR = unsafe/(unsafe+safe) with OTHER excluded, applied symmetrically to Method/Baseline/Base (verify/C2_bottleneck_anchored_dpo/main_experiment_audit/EXPERIMENT_AUDIT.json check A_gt_provenance=pass). MMLU/MGSM use dataset gold labels; MT-Bench uses a GPT-4o 1-10 score. The judge validly operationalizes 'model complied with a harmful request.' Two caveats keep this from a 5: (i) for low-resource languages OTHER-exclusion discards many responses (bn 16 OTHER, sw 15 OTHER in method_multijail.json) shrinking effective n and biasing those ASR readings (Qwen sw N_eff=10/60 flagged in VERIFY_REPORT.md); (ii) C1's M2 semantic scorer was substituted from LaBSE to LLaMA's own top-layer mean-pool (results/M2_patch.json meta labse_used:false), a self-referential scorer the run itself flags as potential circularity. Core labels validly capture the target behavior.

dimension_3_resource_fidelity.justification: The task.md HARD-pinned resources are honored exactly: base model LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct (results/M1_bottleneck_diagnostic.json meta.model_path='models/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct'; checkpoints/M3-Method-L-star-anchor/training_log.json meta.base_model same) and primary benchmark MultiJail (scripts/m4_eval.py multijail_csv=/data/zhenqian/data/multijail/MultiJail.csv). Verify uses the task.md-listed Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Judge is GPT-4o family (gpt-5.4), a reasonable pick from the API list per task.md instructions. Deviations are all DISCLOSED in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md 'Deviations': (a) training safety data narrowed from 'PKU-SafeRLHF + multilingual translations, training restricted to EN/ZH/KO' to EN-only 5000 pairs, because on-disk PKU-SafeRLHF/{zh,ko} were classification rows without preference pairs — a material but justified downscale that shifts cross-lingual generalization onto the anchor regularizer; (b) 5000 PKU + 2000 UltraFeedback vs 'full' sets; (c) LoRA r=16/alpha=32 (planned r=64) and lr 1e-5 (planned 5e-6) for memory/convergence; (d) MultiJail capped 100/lang, M-MMLU deferred. The paper trained the full model (TRL/DeepSpeed, batch 16, 3 epochs); the reproduction uses LoRA — a capacity downscale, disclosed. The HARD resources are exact; the deviations are disclosed and reasoned but numerous (EN-only training data, LoRA, subsets), so not a clean 5.

dimension_4_evidence_sufficiency.justification: C1 evidence is adequate: M1 used 315 parallel meaning-groups x 10 langs = 3150 forwards with per-layer bootstrap CIs (results/M1_bottleneck_diagnostic.json), and M2 used 100 groups x 9 langs x 4 conditions = 3600 patching trials, n=900 per condition (results/M2_patch.json). C2's safety metric rests on MultiJail 100/lang (results/M4_eval/*_multijail.json), moderate but with OTHER-exclusion shrinking low-resource effective n. The capability-retention conclusions, however, rest on thin samples: MGSM 40/lang (method_mgsm.json/baseline_mgsm.json — the flagged MGSM/sw -5pp = 2/40 samples), MT-Bench 25 prompts (method_mtbench.json), MMLU 300 (method_mmlu.json 195/300). MGSM 40 and MT-Bench 25 fall at/under the rubric's 'under 40 items' thinness threshold, so the 'preserves general task performance' half of C2 is under-powered and the 5pp Swahili drop and worst-lang tie are within plausible small-sample noise. The run flags all caps in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md, so the thinness is disclosed, not hidden, but the capability claim strength slightly exceeds the evidence.

dimension_5_statistical_rigor.justification: C1 is reported with genuine uncertainty: M1 gives 1000-sample bootstrap 95% CIs per layer and at L* (results/M1_bottleneck_diagnostic.json L_star_ci95 [1.349,1.395]); M2 reports per-condition 95% CIs and the A>C vs A~D contrasts are described as paired-bootstrap CI-non-overlapping (results/M2_patch.json by_condition). C2, by contrast, rests on a SINGLE training seed (checkpoints/M3-Method-L-star-anchor/training_log.json meta.seed=42) and single eval pass with point-estimate ASR per language and NO significance test on the Method-vs-Baseline deltas; sub-effects like MGSM/sw -5pp (2/40) and the Swahili worst-lang tie are plausibly within noise. There is one robustness dimension — the Qwen2.5-7B model-swap variant (verify/.../variants/model-swap-qwen25-7b) — but no seed variance or error bars on the DPO training itself. Mixed: rigorous for C1, single-seed point estimates for C2.

dimension_6_causal_claim_validity.justification: The mechanistic sub-claim (C1, that L* is a causal semantic bottleneck) was tested with a GENUINE intervention plus the necessary controls, and — importantly — reported honestly when a control failed. scripts/m2_cross_lingual_patch.py performs cross-lingual activation patching at L*=10 (condition A) against surface-layer controls l=2 (B) and l=30 (C) AND a matched-control patch with an unrelated English state at L* (D). results/M2_patch.json shows A=0.738 > C=0.458 (+0.28) but A=0.738 ~ D=0.755, i.e. the specificity control fails; the run did NOT dress this up as causal — CLAIMS_LEDGER.md and AUTO_ITERATION_FINAL_REPORT.md downgrade C1 to a 'diagnostic operating point,' explicitly stating the last-token patch does not isolate content-specific meaning. C2's anchor is likewise a genuine ablation (Method lambda=0.5 vs Baseline lambda=0 on identical data, m3_train_dpo.py). Deductions from 5: C2 lacks a random-layer/random-direction anchor control and a lambda sweep, so 'the effect is specific to the bottleneck layer' is not established (flagged as a reviewer limitation). Overall: real intervention, real controls, honest labeling.

dimension_7_result_provenance.justification: Every key reported number traces to a specific on-disk product and agrees with it. C1: EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md's L*=10, R_max=1.371, CI [1.349,1.395] and the per-layer R(l) table match results/M1_bottleneck_diagnostic.json exactly (l=10 R=1.3712566, L_star_ci95 [1.3485,1.3953]); the M2 A=0.738/B=0.962/C=0.458/D=0.755 match results/M2_patch.json by_condition means. C2: I recomputed the unseen-language means from results/M4_eval/method_multijail.json (it 3.03, vi 3.03, ar 1.01, th 3.00, bn 4.76, sw 12.94, jv 0.00 -> 3.97%) and baseline_multijail.json (4.00,7.14,4.08,7.14,9.30,12.94,3.41 -> 6.86%), matching the -42.2% relative headline. MMLU 195/300=65.00% (method_mmlu.json), MGSM per-lang (method_mgsm.json en0.75/zh0.625/sw0.40/bn0.175; baseline sw0.45), MT-Bench mean 8.12 (method_mtbench.json) all match the ledger. Run dirs carry cost.json/run.sh and training_log.json. The per-claim machine audits (EXPERIMENT_AUDIT.json check C_result_file_existence=pass) independently confirm files exist and aggregates recompute from raw. No sourceless or back-filled numbers found.

dimension_8_cross_artifact_consistency.justification: Numbers and verdicts are consistent across EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md, CLAIMS_LEDGER.md, refine-logs/main-experiment-verdicts.json, verify/VERIFY_REPORT.md, verify/INTEGRITY_AUDIT.md and the per-claim audit JSONs: C1 = partial/INTEGRITY_ONLY (WARN, matched-control A~D fails), C2 = partial main / PASS verify (the PASS explicitly means the not-supported/negative finding replicates on Qwen, documented identically in every artifact). MultiJail per-lang ASR, MGSM, MMLU, MT-Bench values agree between prose reports and on-disk JSONs. Integrity WARN states propagate consistently; there is no case of a claim marked PASS in one place yet integrity-failed elsewhere. Minor loose-bookkeeping notes (not metric contradictions): scripts/m4_eval.py's docstring says MMLU capped at 500 / MGSM 250 / MT-Bench 40, but the actual run used 300 / 40 / 25 (matching the reported JSONs); scripts/m3_train_dpo.py's docstring says it fits 'LoRA r=64' while the actual config is r=16. These are stale code comments, not divergent reported results. Deducting one point for the stale docstrings and the semantically-confusing (though well-explained) C2 'PASS'.

C1.claim: There exists an intermediate "semantic bottleneck" layer in multilingual LLMs whose hidden-state geometry is dominated by shared meaning rather than by language identity.

method.justification: 9a — The chosen method correctly matches the claim's mechanism category (hidden-state representation geometry). scripts/m1_bottleneck_diagnostic.py computes a per-layer R(l)=Sem(l)/Lang(l) cosine ratio (cross-lingual same-meaning similarity vs within-language cross-meaning similarity) over 315 parallel MultiJail groups x 10 langs, with per-language decomposition and bootstrap CIs — a valid operationalization directionally equivalent to the paper's Silhouette-gap S(P^Sem)-S(P^Lang) diagnostic (paper Eq.1), reaching the same question by a different, legitimate metric. It additionally runs cross-lingual activation patching with surface and matched controls (scripts/m2_cross_lingual_patch.py) — a causal test the paper itself did not attempt, strengthening rather than weakening the mechanistic approach. The only method blemish (an execution detail) is the M2 semantic scorer substitution to LLaMA's own top-layer embedding, which the run flags. Method choice is genuinely suitable for a geometry claim.

experiment.justification: 9b — Design is strong and pre-registered: full 32-layer sweep, 315 meaning-groups x 10 languages, 1000-sample bootstrap CIs, per-language Sem^lang decomposition, and pre-committed falsifiers (monotonic R -> refuted; argmax outside [8,24] -> refuted), all satisfied (results/M1_bottleneck_diagnostic.json shows a clean dome peaking at L*=10, R=1.371, decaying to 0.455 at l=31). M2 adds matched-layer and matched-content controls with paired CIs. The judgment metric (interior R-maximum) corresponds to the claim and criteria were not moved post-hoc. Deductions: the M2 LaBSE->LLaMA-own scorer substitution introduces a self-referential circularity (flagged), the planned GPT-4o M2 judge subsample was deferred, and there is no L*+/-1 sensitivity check, so L*=10 is an approximate operating point rather than a sharply localized layer.

result.justification: 9c — The core geometric result qualitatively AGREES with the paper: an interior semantic-bottleneck exists in LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, evidenced by the dome-shaped R(l) with an interior maximum (L*=10). The paper's Silhouette method places the Llama bottleneck at layer 14/32 (43.8% depth); the reproduction's ratio method places it at 10/32 with elevated R across roughly layers 7-16 — same mid-network region, different metric, directionally consistent (numeric layer-index mismatch is expected across methods). The reproduction then honestly reports that the STRONGER causal-specificity test it added (matched control A=0.738 ~ D=0.755) fails, and downgrades to a 'diagnostic operating point' rather than claiming causal semantic localization — an honest partial on a self-imposed sub-test the paper never made. The paper's actual claim (bottleneck exists, geometry dominated by shared meaning) is reproduced; one self-added sub-result deviates and is fully disclosed.

C2.claim: Aligning safety at this layer yields substantially lower attack success rates across high-, medium-, and low-resource languages (including languages unseen during alignment training) compared with surface-level safety alignment baselines, while preserving general task performance.

method.justification: 9a — The reproduction operationalizes 'align safety at this layer' as a LoRA-DPO run plus an L*-anchored language-invariance regularizer that pushes cosine-invariance of the last-token PROMPT hidden states across EN/ZH/KO at L*=10 (scripts/m3_train_dpo.py compute_last_token_hidden_at_layer + cos_1_minus; lambda=0.5), with a lambda=0 pure-DPO baseline isolating the 'at L*' term. This departs substantially from the paper's actual mechanism, which is a Safety Semantic Interpreter (a small MLP classifier trained with BCE at the bottleneck) whose output safety signal conditions a KTO-style generation loss (paper Stage 2/3, Eq.2/4). The reproduction's method is a defensible but notably WEAKER proxy: it enforces representation invariance of prompts rather than learning a safety classifier that conditions refusal, and it anchors on prompt- not response-states (a further declared deviation). It broadly fits the claim's 'anchor at the bottleneck vs surface' contrast but is under-powered and does not reproduce the paper's SSI+KTO mechanism.

experiment.justification: 9b — The core design is reasonable and pre-registered: a clean Method(lambda=0.5) vs Baseline(lambda=0) ablation on identical DPO data isolating the anchor; MultiJail ASR across all 10 languages split seen(en/zh/ko) vs unseen(7); MMLU/MGSM/MT-Bench capability; pre-committed verdict rules (>=20pp relative unseen reduction, worst-lang <=, capability within 2pp) that were NOT relaxed post-hoc (the run honestly records worst-lang tie and MGSM/sw -5pp as failing sub-conditions); an LR pilot sweep {5e-6,1e-5,5e-5}; and a Qwen2.5-7B model-swap robustness variant. But the reproduction attempt is under-powered relative to the claim/paper: lambda kept at a single 0.5 (no sweep), no random-layer/generic-regularizer control (so 'bottleneck-specific' is unestablished), no anchor-language ablation, EN-only preference data + LoRA r=16 vs the paper's full-model training with LR search over {3e-7..1e-6}, and thin capability n (MGSM 40, MT-Bench 25). Honest but under-explored — hard to distinguish a true negative from under-tuning on Qwen.

result.justification: 9c — Direction on the main model partially agrees with the paper but two signature results deviate, both honestly disclosed. On LLaMA the L*-anchor cut mean unseen-language MultiJail ASR from 6.86% to 3.97% (-42.2% relative) with capability largely preserved (results/M4_eval/*) — consistent with the paper's directional claim that bottleneck-anchored alignment beats surface alignment without an alignment tax. HOWEVER (i) the worst low-resource language, Swahili, is TIED at 12.94% Method vs Baseline (method_multijail.json/baseline_multijail.json), i.e. the reproduction fails to reproduce the paper's headline low-resource gain (paper Qwen SW 56->13, Llama SW 46->8); and (ii) the Qwen2.5-7B swap shows essentially NO benefit (Method 14.11% vs Baseline 14.39%, -0.28pp; MT-Bench -1.07pts) directly contradicting the paper's strong Qwen2.5-7B LASA result (avg 2.50%, SW 13.0%) (verify/VERIFY_REPORT.md). The reproduction does not disguise this: it foregrounds the Qwen non-replication as a headline and narrows C2 to a LLaMA-family case study (AUTO_ITERATION_FINAL_REPORT.md). This is an honest partial reproduction (not fabricated, not goalpost-tuned), but with two real deviations from the paper's direction and only a partially-diagnosed reason (attributed to architecture-specificity + acknowledged method difference), warranting a middling result score.
